root_causes.description: The payment service is a leaf dependency exhibiting a flat ~10s (10000ms) p99 server latency with no errors, normal CPU and memory, and no restarts. This injected latency propagates upstream, driving checkout, frontend and frontend-proxy to the same 10000ms p99 ceiling.

evidence.observed_value: payment p99=10000.000 ms (flat, mean=p50=p95=p99=max=10000.000 across window)

evidence.expected_baseline: no cpu saturation; low and flat

evidence.observed_value: user_checkout_single trace duration=34117ms, status=ok; search p95_duration=348073ms, 0 errors

evidence.query_or_id: Updated: Successfully update ObservedGeneration and FailedMessage of resource
evidence.observed_value: only benign 'Updated' events for payment pod; no OOMKilled/BackOff/FailedMount
evidence.expected_baseline: no crash/kill events, rules out pod_crash

root_causes.description: Checkout shows the same flat 10000ms p99, but as a caller of payment it more likely reflects inherited latency from payment rather than an internal fault. Cannot be fully excluded as the injection point.
Frontend and frontend-proxy also show the 10000ms p99 ceiling, but these are the outermost callers and most consistent with propagated downstream latency rather than an injected fault.

evidence.observed_value: frontend p99=10000.000 ms, frontend-proxy p99=10000.000 ms

remediation_steps: Inspect the payment service deployment/config for an injected latency fault (e.g., flagd latency fault or artificial sleep) and remove/disable it.
Restart or roll back the payment service pods to clear the faulted state, then verify payment p99 returns below 100ms.
Add/verify client-side timeouts and circuit breakers between checkout and payment so a slow payment dependency cannot stall checkout and drag frontend p99 to the 10s ceiling.
Monitor payment p99 and checkout p99 dashboards to confirm recovery and prevent recurrence.
